claims.claim_vi: The source describes Brazil, Amazon's build system: a build configuration read as a DAG, a version set per service (a private space of package versions, with a shared default set called live), local builds and a remote package builder that snapshots each build and versions the artifact.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Public build tools also pin the exact versions of dependencies, direct and indirect, in lock files (npm package-lock.json, Cargo.lock); in Go the required versions are in go.mod and go.sum only records hashes for integrity, so it is not a lock file.
claims.verified_by: Kiến thức chung của người biên soạn, chưa đối chiếu lại với trang này trong phiên viết (không mở được trang từ môi trường).

claims.claim_vi: Toy resolver: package A requires B>=1.0 (open constraint); B has 1.0 and 1.1 on day 1. Floating (latest) resolution gives A 1.0 + B 1.1 on day 1 and A 1.0 + B 2.0 on day 2 after B 2.0 is published with a changed call signature, which A cannot build against; resolution from a snapshot taken on day 1 gives A 1.0 + B 1.1 on both days. With an upper bound B<2 the resolver would keep 1.1.
claims.verified_by: Run by the author on 2026-10-19 with a small Python program; a two-package toy model.

claims.claim_vi: Brazil is an internal Amazon tool; no public documentation was found, so everything about it rests on the source article.

design_notes_vi: Một khung bốn bước từ khai báo tới sản phẩm và một khung ghi chú kết quả thử.
source_deviations: The source presents Brazil features (config, version sets, remote builder); the lesson keeps the version-set idea and drops machine-type details.
The lesson adds a floating-versus-pinned experiment and public lock-file analogues, which the source does not contain.
Everything about Brazil rests on the source: no public documentation was found to check it.
